prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The monocular depth map captures the 3D layout of the store across the 5 frames as the camera wearer turns right and tilts the view downward, showing near clothing racks in bright white within arm's reach (0.3 to 1.0 m) against mid-ground figures (0.8 to 2.5 m) and darker receding walls, floors, and doorways (2.5 to 4.0 m). In frame 1 a mannequin stands at about 2.0 to 2.5 m on the right behind the left foreground rack; in frame 2 a person on the bottom left (at roughly 1.0 m, partially out of view) and another person partially occluded behind the central rack on the right (at 1.5 to 2.0 m) stand about 1.5 m apart; and in frames 4 and 5 a person in a dark coat stands 1.5 to 2.0 m ahead to the right and behind the jeans rack while the wearer's own hand appears at 0.3 m in the bottom-right corner of frame 5 grasping the jeans. The map makes it much easier than the motion-blurred RGB to judge continuous metric separation and occlusion boundaries between the foreground racks and the people behind them, though coarse silhouettes only hint that the nearby shoppers face away or sideways rather than looking at the camera wearer. However, the depth map is unreliable on reflective and dark surfaces, flattening the mirror reflection of the camera wearer and companion in frame 3 into the wall plane at 2.5 to 3.0 m and saturating dark doorways and floor corners in frames 1, 2, and 4 to black.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map isolates discrete foreground objects and people on a black background across the sequence, outlining the shopper at the bottom left (around 1.0 m) and the shopper occluded behind the rack on the right (1.5 to 2.0 m) in frame 2, as well as the person walking away on the right in frame 4 and standing behind the jeans rack in frame 5 (1.5 to 2.0 m, facing away from the camera wearer). In frames 4 and 5, it also segments the foreground jeans rack within the camera wearer's arm's reach (0.3 to 0.8 m), visually separating the rack's upper boundary from the person partially occluded behind it. Compared to the RGB strip alone, the masks provide sharp silhouettes for the motion-blurred people in frame 2 and clearly show how the foreground rack overlaps the person in frames 4 and 5, though the black background removes all walls, floors, and distance cues. Furthermore, the map is highly unreliable in classification and object permanence: it mislabels a garment on the frame 1 rack as a suitcase and the jeans rack in frames 4 and 5 as a bicycle, falsely labels the mirror reflections of two people in frame 3, wall-hung pants at the top-left of frame 4, and mannequin legs at the top-left of frame 5 as real people, and misses the racks in frames 1 to 3 and the wearer's hand in frame 5.
descriptions.pose: The body and hand pose map is completely blank (all black) across all 5 frames, failing to render any yellow body skeletons or magenta hand skeletons in the scene. In the RGB context, several people and hands are present—including two shoppers at 1.0 to 2.0 m in frame 2 facing left/downward and right away from the camera wearer, two reflected figures in the mirror at 2.5 to 3.0 m in frame 3, a shopper at 1.5 to 2.0 m walking away toward the right doors in frames 4 and 5, and the camera wearer's own right hand reaching out at 0.3 m in the bottom-right corner of frame 5 to hold jeans on the rack within arm's reach. While a functioning pose map would reveal joint positions, body orientation, and hand contact despite background clutter, this output provides zero spatial information and leaves the scene layout, distances, and relative positions entirely unrepresented. The map is completely unreliable here because heavy occlusion by the foreground clothing racks, severe cropping at the frame borders, motion blur in frame 2, and the close egocentric viewing angle of the wearer's hand in frame 5 cause all body and hand detections to fail.
